added_claims.claim: Dunn Capital, founded about 50 years ago and now in its 51st year, is arguably the longest-running pure trend follower because other pioneers of the same era (e.g. Campbell, Millburn) broadened into other strategies; a half-century live record of one trend approach is evidence of its robustness.

added_claims.testable: partly - long live record exists but is a single manager

added_claims.claim: Without endorsing Elliott wave, Niels flags the scenario that a 'grand super cycle' top is in: years of equities without new highs and a deep bear market, and doubts that investors used to long buy-and-hold are prepared, which favours strategies that can go short.
added_claims.indicator: multi-year equity bear market scenario (Elliott grand super cycle)
added_claims.direction: equities flat to deeply lower for years; long/short strategies favoured
added_claims.conditions: speculative; Elliott wave is not mathematically defined so interpretation is subjective

added_claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen

added_claims.claim: Niels speculates that a major US market high could coincide with the US's 250th anniversary, echoing long generational and empire cycles (Roman, British); Richard later says the world is entering the 'fourth turning' in earnest. Cycle-timing idea with no tested rule.
added_claims.direction: possible major top in US markets around 2026

added_claims.claim: Richard uses the disappearance of 'buy the bounce' posts on social media as an informal sentiment gauge: two weeks earlier they were common, now not, signalling that dip-buying conviction has broken, so rebounds after policy shocks may no longer arrive and whipsaw risk falls.

added_claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen

added_claims.claim: The technology and internet revolution removed borders for data and communication, so agents everywhere now influence each other and the complexity and interconnectedness of the market system has compounded (and will increase with virtual reality and AI), unlike 30 years ago.

corrections.issue: The as-of date '~9 April 2025' is unsupported: Niels says the CTA index numbers are as of Wednesday night of the recording week and the equity and bond numbers as of Thursday (yesterday).
